The fighters

Sworn to the banner

Profiles come straight from BuhurtOS, the permanent record for buhurt fighters. Tap a fighter for their disciplines, record and tournament history.

Fight with the Reavers?

Add your fighter profile

Your profile lives on BuhurtOS and follows you to every tournament. Once the captain approves you, it appears on this page automatically, record and all.

I

Sign in to BuhurtOS

Use Google or your email. It takes a minute and it is free.

II

Ask to join the Reavers

Pick the Red Deer Reavers. The captain gets a notice and approves you.

III

Forge your profile

Add a photo, your disciplines, a short bio and your socials. Results fill in as you compete.

Create my profile My name is already listed Edit my profile

Already on the roster but never signed in? The captain may have added you. Use “My name is already listed” to claim that profile and keep its history. Only your name, photo and the details you choose are shown publicly.

Crew & leadership

Beyond the list

Squires, organizers, coaches and support crew who choose to be featured. Public profiles are always optional.

Team roles

More than one way to be a Reaver

Buhurt needs people inside the armour and people around it. A strong team makes both visible.

In the list

Fighters

Train for melee, duels, demonstrations and competition.

On the rail

Squires

Armour, hydration, repairs and timing to keep fighters in it all tournament day.

Team ops

Organizers

Practices, events, travel, fundraising and keeping the club moving.

Community

Media & support

Photography, video, demos, sponsors, volunteers and outreach.

Team culture

The Reaver’s code

Competitive without being miserable to be around. Standards in training, and standards in how we treat each other.

I

Team before ego

Melee rewards people who do the job the team needs.

II

Progress honestly

Skills, conditioning, contact, armour and competition, all in the right order.

III

Keep showing up

Consistency matters more than looking impressive at one practice.

Want on the roster?

Start at practice

You do not need armour or a combat background. Meet the team and learn what the sport actually feels like.
